subject: Acme - Audit logging capabilities & SOC 2 / security questionnaire
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: James Johnson <jjohnson@acme.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Audit logging capabilities + next steps

Thanks for the call this morning 1 good to meet you both. Quick recap and next steps from our side regarding audit logging and the security questionnaire you circulated:

Summary of ask:
- Confirm Redwood's SOC 2 status and timeline for Type II
- Describe audit logging capabilities: admin activity logs, API request logs, retention, exportability, immutability/tamper evidence
- Confirm GDPR/HIPAA support and available contractual controls (BAA, data residency)
- Fill out Acme security questionnaire and share any supporting artifacts

What I'm sending now:
- Redwood_Audit_Logging_Spec.pdf (attached) 1 overview of log types, retention options, export paths, and immutability controls

Answers / next steps (proposal):
- SOC 2: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type I and is currently undergoing Type II; expected completion Q4 2027. We can share the Type I report and interim controls evidence now.
- GDPR / HIPAA: We support data residency options on Dedicated/Private deployments and offer a BAA for customers handling PHI.
- Audit logs: We collect admin activity (console actions), API request/response logs (token-level), and system events. Logs are exportable to customer S3 or to our secure log-archive with configurable retention.
- Immutability: For Dedicated/Private, we support WORM exports and signed manifests; for hosted customers we provide append-only storage + signed audit manifests and can stream copies to the customer's S3 for extra immutability guarantees.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will attach the completed questionnaire (please see the attached Acme_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx once you reply) and the audit logging spec.
2) Schedule a 30-45 minute technical walkthrough the week of July 5 to review exported logs, retention settings, and KMS options (I suggest looping in your security lead).
3) We'll provide SOC 2 Type I report and a plan/timeline for Type II evidence collection.

Thanks 1 looping in Aditya (technical lead) and Dev (product security) on the thread to join the walkthrough.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[attachment: Redwood_Audit_Logging_Spec.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks Marissa 1 appreciate the recap and the spec. A few follow-ups from our security team (I've attached our questionnaire):

- SOC 2: can you confirm whether your Type II timeline is firm for Q4 2027? We need to map that against our procurement timeline.
- Export: critical that we can export logs to our S3 (us-east-1) with object locking/WORM enabled. Is that supported?
- Retention: our default requirement is 1 year for admin and API logs; can retention be set per-log-type?
- Immutability: do you provide tamper-evidence (signed manifests, chain of custody) for exported archives?
- Access control: who has read access to raw logs at Redwood? We require RBAC and KMS with BYOK option.

I've attached Acme_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx 1 please fill the Audit Logging tab and return.

Thanks 1 James

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 11:05 AM James Johnson <jjohnson@acme.com> wrote:
> - SOC 2: can you confirm whether your Type II timeline is firm for Q4 2027?
> - Export: critical that we can export logs to our S3 (us-east-1) with object locking/WORM enabled. Is that supported?
> - Retention: our default requirement is 1 year for admin and API logs; can retention be set per-log-type?
> - Immutability: do you provide tamper-evidence (signed manifests, chain of custody) for exported archives?
> - Access control: who has read access to raw logs at Redwood? We require RBAC and KMS with BYOK option.

Thanks 1 answering inline below and attaching the completed Audit Logging tab in the questionnaire. See also the Redwood_Audit_Logging_Spec.pdf attached previously.

- SOC 2: Type II target Q4 2027 is our current plan; we will commit to sharing interim evidence and the Type I report immediately. I'll also ask our compliance team for a short roadmap doc.

- Export / WORM: Yes 1 we support exporting logs (full admin and API logs) to customer-owned S3 buckets. For Dedicated/Private we support configuring object lock/WORM on the destination S3. For hosted customers we can stream copies to a customer S3 or export periodic snapshots to an S3 we provision; we can work with your procurement/security to ensure object lock is enabled on the destination.

- Retention: Retention is configurable per log-class (admin, API, system). Default retention is 90 days for hosted, but retention can be extended up to 7 years on Dedicated/Private plans. We'll call out exact retention windows in the questionnaire responses.

- Immutability / tamper-evidence: We provide signed manifests and SHA256 digests for exported archives and optional notarization via append-only manifests. For Dedicated/Private deployments, customers can enable WORM on their export bucket to enforce immutability.

- Access control / KMS: RBAC is enforced in the control plane; access to raw logs at Redwood is limited to the security/admin operations team and audited. We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private and for S3 exports.

Attachments: I've filled the Audit Logging tab in Acme_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx with answers and references to specific pages in Redwood_Audit_Logging_Spec.pdf. Please review; where you'd like more detail we can bring Aditya or Dev into the walkthrough for a demo of the export flow and to show a sample signed manifest.

Proposed times for the technical walkthrough (30-45 min): July 6 (Tue) 10:00-10:45 PT or July 7 (Wed) 14:00-14:45 PT. Which works for your team?

Thanks,
